Humans – Children of Illia
Origins & Spiritual Nature
Humans were created by Illia, the Mother-Goddess, who became obsessively protective of them. They are the only race whose souls are bound to the world, capable of reincarnation and Incarnation—a divine gift that briefly restores memories of past lives.
Their reincarnation cycle is unique: non-human souls return to the Source, but humans reincarnate unless their souls are severed (e.g., by Vitrius or death near a Tear in Reality).
Cultural Traits
Capable of Incarnation (5–12 months, typically between ages 30–50).
Experience visions, dreams, and spiritual restlessness beforehand.
Only during Incarnation can a Branded renew their divine oath.
Factions & Variants
Revalon Humans: Politically and magically advanced. Embrace Incarnation as sacred.
Aphyrians: Stoic warriors. See Incarnation as a burden to endure.
Xanderans: Use Incarnation practically; value its effect on society, not the individual.
Llatherosi: View Incarnation as a grim cycle; dark humor surrounds it.
Rathani: Brutal exiles. Chose survival over reincarnation. See below.
Religious & Political Roles
Central to all God Wars.
Form the Council of the Incarnate.
Many become Branded—divine warriors of Illia.

Rathani – The Forsaken Flame
Origins & Spiritual Nature
The Rathani are humans who, during a desperate age, struck a bargain with Vitrius, severing their souls from reincarnation. In return, they received the Burning Will—a violent, divine fury that grants immense power but rapidly destroys the body.
Upon death, their souls are claimed by Vitrius.
Culture
Tribal, war-driven, and callous.
Society built on raiding, strength, and survival.
Practice ritual blood-painting and cutting before battle.
No centralized state—led by chieftains vying to be High Chief.
Magic
View magic with suspicion and envy.
Do not trust sorcery, but will exploit it for gain.

Valekin – Children of the Great Tree
Origins & Spiritual Nature
Created by Eldymor, the Valekin dwell within the Great Tree (Mavren/Isylathen) in Evervale. The tree is a divine being that sustains them. Their souls return to the Source, but their lives are long (300–400 years), filled with spiritual clarity and innocence.
Physical Traits
Leaflike hair, barklike horn-crests.
Spindly fingers, eyes in seasonal hues.
Culture
Communal, currency-free.
Live within Mavren, sustained by its magic.
Considered sacred by surrounding forest peoples.

Valekin Cousins – (Name TBD)
Origins & Traits
These kin live outside the Great Tree but within Evervale. Unlike the Valekin, they have human-like hair and the power to bond with animals, gaining the ability to shapeshift into that form.
Culture
Nomadic, clan-based (e.g., Clawclan, Antlerclan).
Strong oral tradition: vision dances, seasonal rites.
Breaking the bond causes spiritual and emotional ruin.

Cylvani – Wardens of Evervale
Origins & Spiritual Nature
Centaur-like beings created by Eldymor to guard Evervale and its sacred groves. Serve as border wardens between humans and nature.
Culture
Part of the Keepers of Evervale.
Select trees via spiritual guidance.
Ritualistically honor and “send” the tree’s soul to the Source before felling.
Combat & Trade
Renowned archers and spear fighters.
Provide magical Evervale wood to Revalon; highly limited and precious.

Vulkari: The Forgotten Kin
Core Identity
The Vulkari are a once-human race twisted by Vitrius or his mortal proxies to serve as hunters of dissenters and rebels. Wolf-like in form, primal in instinct, they were designed to obey—then abandoned. Now, they wander the world as memory-haunted beasts, half-feral and half-divine. They remain spiritually tethered to Illia’s reincarnation cycle, suffering a tragic distortion of Incarnation.

Origins & Spiritual Nature
Though their bodies have been corrupted, the Vulkari still reincarnate like humans. During rare celestial events known as the Twin Blood Moons, they transform back into human form—and undergo an accelerated Incarnation, remembering fragments of all past lives, kills, betrayals, and lost names. This painful awakening lasts only a single night, leaving most broken or maddened by grief and guilt.

Cultural Traits & Values
Instinct and Pack: Vulkari structure their society around pack bonds and survival. Loyalty is sacred.
Ritualized Memory: They do not write, but mark bone, bark, and stone with their remembered truths.
Guilt as Sacrament: They revere those who bear memory; pain is holy.
The Blood Moon is sacred and feared—a time of both reckoning and revelation.

Rememberers
Every pack may have a Rememberer—a Vulkari who chooses to hold memory between moons. These individuals are not different in kind, but in will. They inscribe, recite, or carve the stories of their pack, trying to retain humanity across the endless forgetting. They age quickly, often die young, and are revered as living relics of the soul. No one assigns this role—it is claimed in agony and devotion.

Relations with Other Races
Humans: Most humans fear and hunt Vulkari, though few understand their origin or pain.
Animari: View Vulkari as tragic anomalies—proof that Incarnation is not always clean.
Rathani: Some Rathani see them as failed kin; others as sacred martyrs.
Serathi and Nahara’jin: Consider them beasts or tools—never equals.

Role in the God Wars
Originally bred or cursed to serve Vitrius as hunters, many Vulkari were used as shock troops and trackers in the early God Wars. Their usefulness waned as their instincts grew unstable, and they were left to fade into wilderness and ruin. Their continued survival is seen by some as a divine oversight, and by others as a hidden key to the gods’ failures.

Notable Legends & Myth
The Bone-Marked: A Rememberer who carved the story of 27 fallen packmates into his ribs before dying at dawn.
The First Howl: Said to be a Vulkari who, during Incarnation, spoke the name of Vitrius and caused the moon to tremble.
The Mourning Pack: A group of Vulkari who all became Rememberers together, and disappeared into the northern storm without a sound.

Nahara’jin – The Glorious Hunt
Origins
Big cat-like humanoids created by Vitrius. Boastful, proud, and glory-driven.
Culture
Society of Three Prides: Kingdom, House, Household.
Firstborn inherit rulership.
Hunts are sacred rites; death and victory must be witnessed to matter.
Reject Incarnation; prefer glory achieved in a single life.

Serathi – Blood-Daughters of Vitrius
Origins
Serpent-bodied matriarchs of the West. Created by Vitrius and view him as their divine progenitor, the Blood Father.
Beliefs
Death = shedding weakness; rebirth = strength.
Do not keep records. The past is discarded like shed skin.
Matriarchal: Males are viewed as emotional, unintelligent, and good for breeding only.
Power & Culture
Control most of the Western trade and black markets.
Use blood magic and public rituals in worship of Vitrius.
Cities carved into cliffs and mountains (e.g., Pathishar).

Thral’kor – The Broken Giants
Origins
Created by Vitrius as a twisted joke—massive beings made docile and nurturing, used as prey in his monstrous games.
Nature
Innately devoted to Vitrius, even against their will.
Gentle by design, but forced into violence by circumstance.
Many now live in broken clans, raiders, or underhuman alliances.
Tragedy
Cultivate gardens. Avoid harm if possible.
Mocked by other races as “failed giants.”

Undead – Storm-Bound Legion
Origins
Spawned from a ruined kingdom beneath the eternal storm in the West. Initially human, their ambition turned to dark arcana during the God Wars.
Traits
Raise the dead of any who wander too close.
Desire to free Vitrius and trigger another God War.
Seek to raise an army from all past wars.

Dragons – The Silent Flame
Origins
Created by Vitrius, but reject his dominion. Live in the volcanic Burning Islands, formed during the First God War.
Nature
Reclusive, ageless, wise.
View gods as beneath them—unworthy of worship.
Only interfere when their domain is threatened.

 

Cycle of Souls: Doctrine of Rebirth and Incarnation
1. Reincarnation – The Universal Return
All sentient souls in the world of the God Wars are bound to return to the world upon death. This process, known as Reincarnation, ensures that no soul truly escapes the cycle of existence. The Source receives and redistributes non-human souls, while humans and those still bound to the world are returned through different divine mechanisms.

2. Human Incarnation – The Sacred Flame
Humans, created by Illia, are the only race gifted with true Incarnation—a temporary return of past-life memories. Typically occurring once in a lifetime (most often between ages 30–50), Incarnation lasts five to twelve months. During this time, individuals may experience dreams, visions, and behavioral echoes from previous incarnations.
This process is seen as both a divine blessing and a rite of spiritual integration, shaping Revalon’s institutions, religious rites, and culture.

3. Vulkari – The Broken Cycle
Once human, the Vulkari were twisted into beast-like forms through divine corruption. Despite their monstrous condition, their souls remain within the human cycle. Each time the Twin Blood Moons rise, they experience a distorted Incarnation: for one night, they return to human form and are flooded with fragmented memories of all previous lives—every kill, betrayal, and moment of lost humanity.
This process is agonizing and emotionally devastating. Many Vulkari break under its weight, while others rise as Rememberers—those who choose to retain and carry memory between moons.

4. Non-Human Races – Return to the Source
Valekin, Cylvani, Serathi, Nahara’jin, and others reincarnate through the Source. These souls return without Incarnation, usually emerging as new individuals rather than echoes. Their memory may persist through cultural or spiritual patterns but not in a conscious or reclaimable form.

5. Rathani – Severed from the Cycle
The Rathani, once human, made a pact with Vitrius to gain survival in the West. In doing so, they severed their connection to Illia's cycle. Their souls now belong to Vitrius and are bound to his will upon death. While powerful in life through the Burning Will, they are spiritually cursed and cannot reincarnate.

6. Theological Implications
Illia’s gift of Incarnation is unique and deliberate—a thread of divine memory.
Vitrius corrupts but does not erase—his victims still return, but in suffering.
The Source remains a neutral force, allowing life to continue but withholding the depth of human self-awareness.
The Vulkari stand as a living paradox: the soul remembered, the self lost.

 
Revalon: Bastion of Unity
Core Identity
Revalon is a shining emblem of order, unity, and principled governance amidst the fractured powers of the Eastern continent. Though shaped by war and tempered by betrayal, it remains steadfast in its ideals—honor, justice, and the preservation of peace. To its allies, Revalon is a shield against chaos. To its enemies, a stubborn light that refuses to fade.

Founding Principles
Duty Above Self: Every knight, noble, and citizen is bound by the principle that service to the greater good outweighs personal ambition.
Unity in Diversity: Revalon is a melting pot of races, guilds, and spiritual orders. It does not demand sameness, but mutual respect and shared purpose.
Justice Through Wisdom: The law is tempered by understanding. Counsel, scholarship, and moral guidance shape governance as much as arms do.

Government & Structure
Revalon is ruled by a monarch, advised by a High Council made up of knights, temple representatives, and guild delegates. The monarchy is bound by sacred law and may be challenged by the council if honor is betrayed.
The Flameguard serve as its elite defenders and emissaries, revered not merely for skill, but for embodying the kingdom’s highest virtues.

Relations with Other Powers
Llatheros: Bound by royal marriage, the alliance is both spiritual and political. Revalon sees Llatheros as a moral compass.
Xanderon: A pragmatic ally with conflicting methods. Tensions arise, but both kingdoms benefit from shared military and economic strength.
The West: Viewed with deep mistrust. Revalon considers the influence of Vitrius and the fractured Western powers a continual threat to stability.

Cultural Themes
Chivalry and Honor: Knights are held to strict codes of conduct; betrayal is a stain not easily erased.
Templar Wisdom: Revalon respects both martial strength and spiritual discipline. Temples are places of learning and moral reflection.
Legacy and Duty: Bloodlines matter, but so does merit. Many of Revalon’s greatest heroes were not born noble, but proved themselves in service.


 
God Wars World Guide

1. Pantheon & Cosmology

Eldymor â€“ The Gardener God / The Father:

Vitrius â€“ The God of Will / The Blood Father:

- Creations: Monsters, giants, dragons, undead, Vulkari, Serathi, Naharaâ€™jin, Rathani.

- The Serathi worship him as a god; the Rathani revere him for their survival.


2. Historical Timeline

- Illia creates the first humans.
- Eldymor creates animals, the Great Tree, and spiritual life.
- Vitrius creates monsters, giants, dragons. Conflict begins.

- Illia reincarnates them, binding their souls to the world.
- World is split: East (humans, Valekin, Cylvani), West (Vitriusâ€™ creations).
- Central volcano forms, becomes the dragon's domain.

Second God War â€“ The Reckoning of Roots:
- Illia and Vitrius wage war.
- Eldymor returns to help repel Vitrius.

Seventh & Eighth God Wars:

3. Geography & Regions

The world consists of two major continents, a central archipelago, and submerged civilizations.

- Dominated by humans, Valekin, Cylvani, and related groups.
- Revalon: Cultural and political capital, powered by reincarnation traditions and magical institutions like the Skyward Temple.
- The Great Tree (Mavren): A divine entity that houses the Valekin; a spiritual and physical heart of the East.
- Evervale: Also known as the Sea of Trees, protected by the Cylvani.
- Myndwynn: Sacred forest lands where the Cylvani regulate tree harvests through divine guidance.

- Home to the dragons; isolated and mysterious.

A Nahara’jin who, according to his slurred introduction, had just immigrated to Revalon from the Lower Islands after fleeing his homeland. The surprisingly amicable cat-folk were an imposing sight in any situation. But when their livers are drowned in mug after mug of mead, they are a different creature entirely and forget that they are among humans.
By the time Addicus had arrived, the beast was standing over three fallen, bloody men, waving his mug in the air and singing a song in what must have been his native tongue. Addicus had to enlist Farthing, the closest guard, to help him drag the singing, stinking mass to the prison tower—three more were needed to secure him in his cell.
The two bickering men in front of Addicus now—they were homegrown Revalonians. He remembered seeing the bald, red-bearded man only hours earlier, begging in the town square. He pitifully wailed to anyone passing in earshot that he was a pius man, cursed by the gods, and needed only a full stomach. It would seem, Addicus thought, it wasn’t food he was speaking of.
The other one Addicus didn’t recognize; he must have been from one of the other duchies. He was a slightly younger looking man with his jet black hair tied up in a knot. He was within inches of the beggar’s face, his index finger jabbed into the man’s chest repeatedly as accusations flew like Cylvani arrows.

They ignored him. The black-haired man was determined to settle the matter, raising a sloppy fist and swinging a sloppy punch. As his arm swung around his legs forgot to follow and he collapsed onto the floor like a sack of horse feed.
The foreigner moved towards the downed bald man but was cut off by Addicus, who held him back as he cursed at the beggar.
“Enough!” declared Addicus. “Or I’ll haul off both of you.”
Unbothered by the beleaguered guard’s assertion, the pious drunkard, who had returned surprisingly quickly to his feet, lumbered towards the duo, blood running down the right side of his neck, due to his unceremonious landing.
“Dammit I was fending off islanders when you were still pissin’ your bed. I’ll show you how the Iron line fight, you disrespectful goat-prick.”
As Addicus braced himself for the enraged burly man who was now inches away, the Revalonian retorted from behind, “Dogpiss. My uncle was the captain of the Iron Line when the islanders tried to take the south.”
“For the last time…” Addicus started, but was cut off by the bald man.
“Now who’s a lying cunt. Captain Fraderic would never abide a nephew the likes of you.”

“Fraderick Duranson?”
The look of surprise was infectious as the beggar’s eyes opened wide in disbelief. “Aye, the old man could cut down a dozen men at once.”
A small smile crept to the lips of the Revalonian. “And then drink them all under the table!”
Addicus lowered his hands as the two men looked at each other as if for the first time. “Right, great. Now...” Addicus started before being interrupted by the beggar.
“That he could!” He laughed heartily as the blood from his ear continued dropping to the dirty tavern floor in red spots.
The beggar paused for a moment, as if his mead-soaked mind were grasping for a distant thought. “Let me buy you a mug, nephew of the Iron Line!”
The Revalonian graciously considered the beggar’s offer. “Aye, but the mug’s on me. Anyone that served with Fraderic is a friend of mine.” He clapped the beggar’s shoulder and the two stumbled a path towards a table in the corner of the tavern and away from Addicus, who stood in place for a spell, wrapping his head around what had just happened.
Rolling his eyes, Addicus walked back to the barkeep who had also witnessed the spectacle. “Do you want them out?” he asked, wiping at a new red stain on his tabard and gesturing towards the two newfound friends who were laughing hysterically.
The barkeep, a man called Fritt, must have noticed the weariness in Addicus’ voice. “I doubt they’ll be much of a bother now.”
Addicus nodded his head and turned to leave.
“I get the distinct feeling that you could do with a spirit or two,” Fritt said with a smirk.
Addicus smiled politely. “No thanks, Fritt. On duty, you know.”

“Well how was it then?” he asked as Addicus approached.
“Drunk fools, same as always.” Addicus stopped a few feet from Farthing, admiring an artisan’s handwoven tapestry hanging from a nearby market stall. It was an impressive work—obviously the hand of an Incarnate, judging by the intricate layering of golden and crimson thread.
“Get to knock any heads around?” Farthing never met a duty he hadn’t shirked, but he took a keen interest in any opportunity for violence, which came frequently in the guard post.
“It didn’t quite come to that,” Addicus replied quietly, still looking at the tapestry, imagining himself within the lush beauty and warmth of the Lady’s Garden, standing vigil at her holy statue as a Revalonian knight, only a few hundred paces or so from unholy The Tear itself.

Addicus sighed to himself. “Of course,” he said under his breath as he took his post.
The rising sounds of hammers followed by saws meant that repairs on the southwest bridge were well under way.
Most passerbys are oblivious of a guard standing at his post. This doesn’t apply to the South District, however. Here, a guard is under constant watchful eyes.
Even as a slew of people passed Addicus, he saw that familiar look—a mixture of anger and distrust—that Southenders seemed to wear like a mask.
The central square was a hodgepodge of the desperate sales pitches of merchants, the low but constant humming of beggars’ pleas, and the raucous laughter of children and drunkards alike.
It was a place all too easy to get lost in—indeed, that’s why some of the more criminal elements preferred the cover of the district’s shadow.
It certainly was no desired posting among the guard. As the youngest and newest addition, Addicus was naturally saddled with the duty fairly routinely. Pl...please, rise ma'am." Renning said, both hands grasping the outreaching spinstress's shaking hands.

For the first time of the day, his words were heeded. The conjectures turned to hush whispers as the crowd dispersed, leaving only the Animari, save the still-weeping old women and a young anxious woman at her side.
